text.p: These are the leading stories in Albania's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The paper's editorial says President Sali Berisha indirectly made it clear yesterday he would quit after he nominated a prime minister to his liking.
- Berisha said he would convene parliament after the final election results are issued and then he would resign.

- Final election results cannot be issued because President Sali Berisha heads the proportional list of his defeated Democratic Party. Socialist members of the electoral commission claim he should resign before receiving a parliamentary mandate.
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky warned the international community would boycott Albania unless its politicians assumed their responsibilities after the June 29 elections.
- Residents of the northern town of Shkoder, an important former industrial and trade centre, are unhappy no one from their town has been picked as a member of the new government.
- Albanian politics is a men's job: there are 148 men in parliament and only eight women.

- Italian authorities have launched an appeal to police about the possible child organ traffic from Albania. Doctors both in Italy and Albania doubt the highly sophisticated operation could take place in Albania.

- U.S. ambassador to Tirana Marisa Lino has told Republican Party chairman Sabri Godo Albania would receive American aid once the political situation is unblocked and the new government starts working.
- The Democratic Party will boycott the first session of parliment and it will also boycott all those sessions that would discuss major constitutional changes.
